title: Hiccups and sneezing: normal newborn quirks?
summary: Frequent hiccups and sneezes are usually normal reflexes, not illness.
whatsNormal:
Newborns have immature nervous and digestive systems, quirky sounds are common.

• Hiccups: often after feeds or when belly is full; harmless if baby is comfortable
• Sneezing: clears nose of mucus and dust; not the same as allergy sneezing in older kids
• Stuffy nose without fever is common, saline drops and gentle suction if needed
• Periodic breathing (short pauses) can be normal in sleep, ask your clinician what to watch for

Neither hiccups nor sneezing alone usually means your baby is sick.
watchFor: Hiccups with forceful vomiting every time
Sneezing with thick green discharge, fever, or poor feeding
Breathing faster than usual, grunting, or nostrils flaring
Blue or gray color around lips during feeds or after sneezing fits
callDoctorIf: Breathing difficulty or pauses that worry you, video for your clinician helps
Signs of dehydration or refusing feeds
You cannot tell normal quirks from illness, call; that is OK
